quick_answers.question: Did the bosonic parent work?
quick_answers.answer: Yes, in the scoped BGG (X,T,Y) kinetic block.

quick_answers.question: Did the specified strict off-shell FLRW SUSY truncation work?
quick_answers.answer: No; two independent normal-mode coefficients are nonzero at an exact clean point.

quick_answers.question: Can a standard local Q exchange t<0 and t>0 support?
quick_answers.answer: No; support locality makes both cross blocks zero.

quick_answers.question: What remains promising?
quick_answers.answer: A fundamental doubled-sheet algebra and a separate doubled-real projector witness exist, but their common action, domain, charge, and physical sheet anchor are open.

quick_answers.question: Does elapsed time itself break supersymmetry?
quick_answers.answer: No in the conserved-charge control: a Q-annihilated state remains Q-annihilated when [H,Q]=0.

quick_answers.question: Can one free instantaneous canonical seam explain missing superpartner pole masses?
quick_answers.answer: No in the frozen Phase 18 class. It can prepare a non-SUSY state, but the post-post retarded B/F poles remain degenerate and a sharp local kick has divergent energy density.

quick_answers.question: Do the displayed closed SUGRA models admit 50–60 accelerated e-folds?
quick_answers.answer: Yes conditionally: six k=+1 homogeneous target-shot background solutions pass the exact turning-point and numerical constraint checks.

quick_answers.question: Does time symmetry now predict phi0, universe size, or a present SUSY spectrum?
quick_answers.answer: No. The bosonic symmetry data leave phi0 free; the radius is conditional, and the displayed stabilizer F directions vanish at their endpoints.

quick_answers.question: Does the leading two-sheet WDW control select phi0=5.442969?
quick_answers.answer: No in the scoped constant-field de Sitter envelope. The standard exp(2sI) history weight and the conditional exp(4sI) independent-pair joint probability are both monotone, but this is not an exact two-sheet SUGRA WDW no-go.

quick_answers.question: Is the Phase 20 curvature–reheating number a seam prediction?
quick_answers.answer: No. The displayed Omega_K0–T_reh conversion is reproducible only after fixing the Phase 19 branch, reheating history, units, and late-time inputs.

quick_answers.question: Does a connected two-sheet Gaussian automatically produce a physical flux probability?
quick_answers.answer: No. Decoupled-sheet normalization identifies the unit baseline, a chosen zero-insertion exclusion gives R-1, and log R is the connected vacuum generator. A flux measure, state prescription, and decoherence rule are still missing.

quick_answers.question: Does the finite-mode density control construct a full CPT/Pin supergravity seam state?
quick_answers.answer: No. For beta,omega>0 it constructs a normalized TFD-like oscillator purification, a finite graded anti-linear real structure, and elementary SK normalization. The 4D Pin lift, physical projector, and local-SUGRA ghost-completed kernel remain open, while the unregulated noncompact omega=0 limit diverges.

quick_answers.question: Does the Phase 23 constraint alone determine a physical cosmological seam density?
quick_answers.answer: No. Full-lapse averaging gives a distributional rigging map, an explicit clock and branch give a positive integrated norm, and a separately supplied compact bridge gives a regulated trace-class density. CPT-like reality and zero signed current do not select its weights, and the massless decompactification limit is not trace class.
